scope: New registry/proposals/ entry (registry/proposals/flood_edge_direction.json, PROP-FLOOD-04, 'Edge head-gradient direction readout ... with refusal'): one method-domain (M) proposal for a community flood-readout application (FloodConnect), via the governed proposals-lane intake process -- NOT promoted into registry/CANONICAL.json, which requires the full schema/lineage/checker workflow this entry has not gone through. PROP-FLOOD-04 is a SPATIAL edge head-gradient direction readout from the head difference between two adjacent gauged nodes of a declared canal graph (Delta_e(t) := h_u(t) - h_v(t)), evaluated as a TOTAL function with refusal rows checked BEFORE direction rows in a fixed precedence (UNDECLARED_EDGE > MISSING_INPUT/STALE_INPUT > DATUM_MISMATCH > CONTROL_STATE_MISSING/CONTROLLED > {u->v, v->u, UNRESOLVED}), a per-gauge resolution threshold epsilon_u+epsilon_v (not a single shared epsilon), and six REFUSED reason codes (MISSING_INPUT, STALE_INPUT, DATUM_MISMATCH, UNDECLARED_EDGE, CONTROLLED, CONTROL_STATE_MISSING) that emit no direction at all. Cites delta_R (instance_of), PROP-FLOOD-01 (spatial_instance_of, the sibling temporal lag-k retained-difference sign readout -- with an explicit note flagging that PROP-FLOOD-02 uses the token 'UNRESOLVED' as a REFUSED reason code while here it is a determinate readout class, to avoid conflating the two) and weld/M.01.v1 / CAN-001 (edge_term_instance_of the L_R = D_W - W row-action edge term, with an explicit caveat that sign(W_uv(x_u-x_v))=sign(x_u-x_v) only for W_uv>0 and that L_R does not imply water flows) as parents, all quoted/cited, not restated as new theorems. Genesis compatibility also cites readout_genesis's Gate 2 Three-Valued Admissibility (READOUT_GENESIS_CORE.md lines ~3768-3776), mapping UNRESOLVED to Genesis's bottom/unresolved value and each determinate REFUSED reason to Genesis's obstructed value. The entry is tier Dr / status unverified, carries a definitions block and explicit claim_boundary/honest_caveats disclaiming any hydrological/flow-rate model content, and empirical_test_status is 'none'. No claim about the Clay Millennium Navier-Stokes problem, or about any object's Clay/NS status, is made or implied anywhere in this change; the status of every existing Clay-related registry object (CANONICAL.json, coq/, docs/CLAY_*) is unchanged -- this PR touches no such object, only adds one new proposals-lane file.
